punchline: The first words of Kabat-Zinn's definition are "on purpose", and noticing that you drifted already counts as practice.
thirty_sec: Jon Kabat-Zinn defines mindfulness as paying attention on purpose, in the present moment, and without judging. The book says much of life runs on automatic and many moments pass unlived. His suggestion is plain: in the shower, over a meal, with a child, do one thing at a time. One of its kinder lines says that forgetting to be mindful can teach you more than always being mindful. So the moment you catch yourself drifting is the practice, not a failure of it.
